subject: Post-demo: SOC 2 Type II packet, bridge letter & secure intake access

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: SOC 2 Type II packet, bridge letter & secure intake access

Hi Liz — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on our demo and the security questions you raised:

- SOC 2 status: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II in Oct 2025; we can share the report under NDA or via our secure intake portal.
- Bridge letter: we can provide a short bridge/attestation addendum that clarifies coverage dates and scope for your auditors.
- Portal: we use a secure intake site (read-only access for review; upload allowed for DSQs) and offer an SFTP fallback for large artifacts.

Action items I can take now:
1) Share a redacted SOC 2 Type II summary and a sample bridge letter (we typically send the full report via the intake portal).
2) Provision short-term access to the secure intake (48–72 hour window) for your security team.
3) Loop in our Compliance lead to answer any scope questions (GDPR/HIPAA/data residency).

Can you confirm: 1) who should get portal access (names + emails) and 2) whether you need a temporary attestation instead of the full report for procurement?

If it helps, I can get a provisioning link to you by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_bridge_letter_sample.pdf (sample bridge letter, redacted), soc2-t2-redwood-2025-summary.pdf (summary of scope/results)

Thanks, Aditya — helpful recap. Please provision access for:
- Tom Blake <tom.blake@insurely.com> (security lead)
- Security team inbox: security@insurely.com

Procurement will accept either the redacted SOC 2 Type II or a temporary attestation plus bridge letter for initial vendor review. Ideally we’d get the bridge letter and portal access within 48 hours — we’re on a bit of a compressed timeline for a late-May procurement decision.

One question: does the SOC 2 scope include encryption at-rest for customer data and the option to restrict data residency to US regions? Also we need to confirm whether you accept our vendor DDQ (attached as a doc) or prefer we fill your standard DSQ.

—Liz
Liz Carter
Sr. IT Risk Manager | Insurely
liz@insurely.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liz Carter <liz@insurely.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SOC 2 Type II packet, bridge letter & secure intake access

Hi Liz — Marissa from Compliance here. Nice to meet you (virtually). Quick answers and next steps: 

1) SOC 2 scope: our Type II report (2025 coverage window) includes control coverage for encryption at-rest and in-transit. Data residency: hosted deployments can be restricted to US-only regions; we’ll confirm the specific region controls for your proposed environment.

2) Bridge letter: I’ve attached a sample bridge letter we can sign and notarize if required. In urgent cases we can provide a temporary attestation addendum that summarizes control continuity between report periods — this is commonly accepted by procurement teams for initial review.

3) Portal access: I just provisioned a temporary reviewer link for Insurely (48-hour access). You should receive an invite from trust@redwoodinference.com; I’ve added the invite URL below. If you prefer SFTP, we can enable that as a fallback and share credentials via our secrets manager.

Next steps for Insurely (please confirm by reply):
- Confirm Tom Blake and security@insurely.com are the accounts to invite.
- Indicate if you want the redacted full report or the attestation + bridge letter combo for procurement.
- If you have a DDQ template, either attach here or paste a link — we’ll route to our security engineering team.

Invite link (temporary): https://trust.redwood-inference.com/intake/INVITE-AB12CD
Portal note: we log all downloads and provide an audit trail; if you need exportable audit logs we can include that in the access package.

Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: redwood_bridge_letter_sample.pdf, secure-intake-invite.html
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2026 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SOC 2 Type II packet, bridge letter & secure intake access

Thanks all — Connor from Security here. Follow-up items I’ll own:

- If Insurely sends the DDQ as an attachment or a link, I’ll start the DSQ pass and flag any technical clarifications (expected turnaround ~2–3 business days for standard vendor DDQs).
- For the portal: I confirmed the temporary invite was sent to tom.blake@insurely.com and security@insurely.com at 09:10 PST this morning. The invite includes the redacted SOC 2 Type II summary and a signed bridge letter PDF.
- If you need the full report under NDA, we’ll send DocuSign for a redaction NDA and then upload the report to the portal.

On the data residency/encryption notes: encryption at-rest is AES-256; key management is via customer-integrated KMS for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS with options for BYOK on Dedicated plans. I’ll add a short one-pager to the portal describing key management options.

Small logistics: if you don’t see the invite, check spam and allowlist trust@redwoodinference.com; otherwise I’ll reissue and enable SFTP.

Connor O'Brien
Security Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com
